what: Cross-validate a random forest by speaker — cv_speakers
title: Cross-validate a random forest by speaker — cv_speakers
text: Splits speakers k folds, fits random forest ranger folds one, predicts tokens speakers left , every token predicted forest never saw speaker. estimates accuracy new speakers, --bag accuracy overestimates tokens speaker alike.

title: Cross-validate a random forest by speaker — cv_speakers
code: cv_speakers(   formula,   data,   speaker = "speaker",   k = 5,   seed = 2,   num_trees = 500 )

title: Cross-validate a random forest by speaker — cv_speakers
text: formula Formula forest, l1 ~ vot + vowel_ratio + rate. data data frame one row per token. speaker Name column speakers, string. k Number folds. seed Seed assigning speakers folds breaking ties votes trees. forest fold uses seed . random seed left . num_trees Number trees forest.

title: Cross-validate a random forest by speaker — cv_speakers
text: tibble one row per token columns speaker, fold, observed predicted. accuracy new speakers mean(cv$predicted == cv$observed).

title: Cross-validate a random forest by speaker — cv_speakers
text: response factor one value per speaker, L1, fold gets number speakers group. default seed, folds forests ones slides Advanced Statistics, session 6.

title: Cross-validate a random forest by speaker — cv_speakers
code: if (requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(simling)   cv <- cv_speakers(l1 ~ vot + vowel_ratio + rate, accent, num_trees = 100)   mean(cv$predicted == cv$observed) } #> [1] 0.875

what: Partial dependence of a model on one predictor — partial_dependence
title: Partial dependence of a model on one predictor — partial_dependence
text: Sets one predictor value every row data, predicts, averages predictions, repeats value (Friedman, 2001). Plotted values, result shows predictions change predictor, averaged predictors. Used Advanced Statistics random forests ranger, works model predict() method.

title: Partial dependence of a model on one predictor — partial_dependence
code: partial_dependence(model, data, var, values, class = NULL)

title: Partial dependence of a model on one predictor — partial_dependence
text: model fitted model. classification forest ranger, fit probability = TRUE. data data predict , usually data model fitted . var Name predictor, string. values Values predictor set, seq(18, 80, = 2). factor, levels factor. class models predict probability class: class whose probability average, "deleted".

title: Partial dependence of a model on one predictor — partial_dependence
text: tibble one row per value columns value prediction, mean prediction (probability class).

title: Partial dependence of a model on one predictor — partial_dependence
text: Friedman, J. H. (2001). Greedy function approximation: gradient boosting machine. Annals Statistics, 29(5), 1189–1232.

title: Partial dependence of a model on one predictor — partial_dependence
code: library(simling) m <- lm(rt ~ log_freq * length, data = megastudy) partial_dependence(m, megastudy, "length", 3:12) #> # A tibble: 10 × 2 #>    value prediction #>    <int>      <dbl> #>  1     3       724. #>  2     4       736. #>  3     5       749. #>  4     6       762. #>  5     7       775. #>  6     8       787. #>  7     9       800. #>  8    10       813. #>  9    11       826. #> 10    12       838.  if (requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE)) {   rf <- ranger::ranger(deleted ~ following + morph + rate + age, data = td_deletion,                        num.trees = 200, probability = TRUE, seed = 1)   partial_dependence(rf, td_deletion, "age", seq(20, 80, by = 10), class = "deleted") } #> # A tibble: 7 × 2 #>   value prediction #>   <dbl>      <dbl> #> 1    20      0.671 #> 2    30      0.644 #> 3    40      0.680 #> 4    50      0.600 #> 5    60      0.514 #> 6    70      0.497 #> 7    80      0.410

what: Autocorrelation of residuals within groups — resid_acf
title: Autocorrelation of residuals within groups — resid_acf
text: Computes autocorrelation model residuals within trajectory, time series group, lags 0 max_lag. lag 1 correlation residual residual one measurement earlier group; lag 2 skips one measurement, . Residuals never paired across groups. Used Advanced Statistics check GAMMs autocorrelated residuals; itsadug::acf_resid() base R graphics.

title: Autocorrelation of residuals within groups — resid_acf
code: resid_acf(res, group, max_lag = 8)

title: Autocorrelation of residuals within groups — resid_acf
text: res Residuals model, residuals(m). group trajectory series residual belongs , data$traj. max_lag largest lag, measurements.

title: Autocorrelation of residuals within groups — resid_acf
text: tibble one row per lag columns lag acf. autocorrelation lag 0 always 1.

title: Autocorrelation of residuals within groups — resid_acf
text: residuals must order data, sorted time within group, res group must length: model dropped rows missing values, drop group .

title: Autocorrelation of residuals within groups — resid_acf
code: library(simling) # a straight line through the PRICE trajectories: the residuals of # neighbouring measurements are strongly correlated m <- lm(f2 ~ time, data = price_f2) resid_acf(residuals(m), price_f2$traj) #> # A tibble: 9 × 2 #>     lag   acf #>   <int> <dbl> #> 1     0 1     #> 2     1 0.887 #> 3     2 0.647 #> 4     3 0.370 #> 5     4 0.164 #> 6     5 0.108 #> 7     6 0.178 #> 8     7 0.269 #> 9     8 0.307

title: konstats (development version)
text: First version. Installing konstats installs packages Statistics course; install_course("advanced") installs extra packages Advanced Statistics, course_packages() lists . check_setup() checks version R packages course. follow, data sets use slides; slides() opens slides lecture. tutorials() lists exercise sheets get_tutorial() copies one project folder. Sheets Statistics tutorials 2 4. R Markdown template weekly assignments. helpers Advanced Statistics slides: resid_acf() (residual autocorrelation within trajectories), partial_dependence() (called partial() slides), cv_speakers() (cross-validation random forest speaker, folds slides) theme_paper().
